Trong buổi học đầu tiên, nhóm tôi có bốn: In our first class, four of us prepared a presentation together. I compiled the content but shared it just before the meeting, leaving two teammates too little time to comment.
In our first class, four of us prepared a presentation together.
Tôi lo lắng khi nhóm im lặng và nghĩ rằn: I felt anxious when the group stayed quiet and assumed they were not interested. After asking, I learned they had not had time to read the material. My unclear communication and task assignments were partly responsible.
I felt anxious when the group stayed quiet and assumed they were not interested.
Tôi học được rằng sự im lặng không đồng: I learned that silence does not mean a lack of responsibility. Asking before drawing conclusions helps me check my assumptions and understand what each teammate needs.
I learned that silence does not mean a lack of responsibility.
Trước buổi học tiếp theo, tôi sẽ gửi bản: Before our next class, I will share a draft two days early and ask each teammate for one suggestion. I will record how many replies I receive to check whether this approach works better.
Before our next class, I will share a draft two days early and ask each teammate for one suggestion.
Lắng nghe phản hồi sau thuyết trình: Listening to feedback after a presentation
DEMO · Lắng nghe phản hồi sau thuyết trì: DEMO · Listening to feedback after a presentation
Sau phần thuyết trình, giảng viên nhận x: After our presentation, the lecturer said our examples were not clearly connected to the theory. I wrote down three suggestions and discussed them with the group at the end of class.
After our presentation, the lecturer said our examples were not clearly connected to the theory.
Ban đầu tôi thấy thất vọng vì đã dành nh: At first I felt disappointed because I had spent so much time preparing. Comparing the feedback with our slides, I saw that I had prioritized appearance over reasoning. The audience needed to understand the connection, rather than simply see attractive images.
At first I felt disappointed because I had spent so much time preparing.
Tôi nhận ra chất lượng bài trình bày khô: I realized that preparation time alone does not measure presentation quality. Feedback gives me evidence to improve my learning, and I need to find support for each argument.
I realized that preparation time alone does not measure presentation quality.
Trong bài tiếp theo, tôi sẽ kiểm tra từn: For our next presentation, I will check each slide by asking what its example demonstrates. We will rehearse with another student and record two points that remain unclear before submitting.
DEMO · Nhận diện cảm xúc khi có bất đồng: DEMO · Recognizing my feelings during disagreement
Khi nhóm chọn hướng nghiên cứu, tôi muốn: When choosing our research approach, I proposed surveying students while a teammate suggested interviewing lecturers. I interrupted twice, and our discussion ran long without reaching a decision.
When choosing our research approach, I proposed surveying students while a teammate suggested interviewing lecturers.
Tôi thấy khó chịu vì sợ phương án của mì: I felt frustrated because I feared my proposal would be overlooked. That feeling came from a need for recognition, rather than only concern about the quality of our approach. My teammate had a reasonable concern that a survey would lack depth.
I felt frustrated because I feared my proposal would be overlooked.
Tôi từng mặc định bảo vệ ý kiến thật mạn: I used to assume that strongly defending my opinion was the best contribution I could make. This experience challenged that assumption: listening and comparing clear criteria can lead to a better decision than trying to win an argument.
I used to assume that strongly defending my opinion was the best contribution I could make.
Ở cuộc họp tuần tới, tôi sẽ tóm tắt ý ki: At our next meeting, I will summarize my teammate's view before responding. We will agree on three criteria for choosing an approach, and afterward I will ask a teammate for feedback on how well I listened.
At our next meeting, I will summarize my teammate's view before responding.
Tìm nguyên nhân khi trễ kế hoạch: Understanding why our plan fell behind

Nhóm dự kiến hoàn thành khảo sát vào thứ: We planned to finish our survey by Friday but had received only half the responses we needed. I was responsible for tracking progress but checked only on the final day, so I did not notice the shortfall early.
We planned to finish our survey by Friday but had received only half the responses we needed.
Tôi cảm thấy áp lực và ban đầu đổ lỗi ch: I felt under pressure and initially blamed the survey participants. Looking back at our invitation schedule, I saw that we had allowed no time for reminders or clear task ownership. My late progress check was also part of the problem.
I felt under pressure and initially blamed the survey participants.
Tôi hiểu rằng một kế hoạch cần có điểm k: I learned that a plan needs checkpoints along the way, rather than only a final deadline. This also applies to my own studying: reviewing results only at the end of the week leaves little time to correct mistakes.
I learned that a plan needs checkpoints along the way, rather than only a final deadline.
Tuần tới tôi sẽ tạo hai mốc kiểm tra vào: Next week, I will set checkpoints on Tuesday and Thursday, record the response count, and alert the group if we are below target. After a week, we will compare our progress and adjust how we send reminders.
Next week, I will set checkpoints on Tuesday and Thursday, record the response count, and alert the group if we are below target.

DEMO · Nhìn tình huống từ góc độ khác: DEMO · Seeing a situation from another perspective
Một thành viên thường vắng cuộc họp tối: A teammate often missed our evening meetings, slowing down the project. I asked why instead of continuing to complain in the group chat. They explained that they worked a part-time job at that time.
A teammate often missed our evening meetings, slowing down the project.
Tôi thấy ngại vì từng cho rằng bạn không: I felt embarrassed because I had assumed they did not care about the project. From their perspective, the schedule chosen by the majority created a barrier. I need to distinguish between being unable to participate and not wanting to participate.
I felt embarrassed because I had assumed they did not care about the project.
Tôi học được rằng công bằng không nhất t: I learned that fairness does not always mean asking everyone to work at the same time. However, I still need to work out how to balance individual circumstances with the group's deadlines.
I learned that fairness does not always mean asking everyone to work at the same time.
Tôi sẽ trao đổi thêm với nhóm về lịch họ: I will talk with the group about our meeting schedule and try a new time. Then I want to see whether more teammates can participate.
I will talk with the group about our meeting schedule and try a new time.
